alternatives.argument: A complete local alternative is in the current theorem: deterministic scalar dual/profile and feasible finite-window construction supply the correctly qualified relaxed extremal power; a concentrated finite three-point prior, direct finite-array Gaussian replacement and scalar likelihood truncation yield sharp lower bounds; a centered-cosh score union a coordinate maximum event yields uniform Gaussian upper bounds with explicit large-amplitude deletion. The final least-dyadic diagonal globalizes the actual test family for small, transition, large and oscillating ratios with exact-level adjustment. The lambda≤0 branch uses a deterministic maximum bound and truncated signed single-spike mixture to prove both sharp error profiles and the exact normalization, including lambda=0. No unread book proof is a premise.

The existing special case q=1,alpha=beta=1 proves its own rate: finite signed-location alternatives have vanishing mixture second moment below epsilon^(1/2)log(epsilon^(-1))^(1/4); a finite-coordinate maximum test plus the weighted-budget tail bound is uniformly consistent above that scale. Its current source body does not cite the 2003book, and it invokes no full sharp sparse theorem. This is the existing local example argument, not a claim to have read a book proof.
